summary: Over 1 Jan 2024 – 30 Jun 2024 (121 trading days), this strategy took 87 trades. Its largest fall from a peak was ₹16,363, its longest run of losing trades was 8 trades, and its single biggest loss was −₹3,683.

In total it would have made ₹7,729 after ₹5,400 in costs, a 7.73% return on the ₹1,00,000 capital you entered. 44.8% of trades made money; the average winning trade made ₹2,175 and the average losing trade lost ₹1,606.
It did best when India VIX was below 12 (on average ₹581 per trade over 10 trades) and worst on call trades (−₹154 over 43 trades).
This period doesn't include both the earlier tuning years and the unseen recent years, so overfitting can't be checked. Choose a longer period to see this check.
If volatility had been 2 points lower, the result would have been ₹24,293; 2 points higher, ₹1,657.
simulation_notes: Entries fill at the open of the minute after the signal candle closes (or at the fixed entry time).
Stop-loss and target are checked every minute; if both are reached in the same minute, the stop-loss is assumed to come first.
Positions still open at expiry are settled at intrinsic value, using the expiry day's last minute.
Strikes are chosen from the index level at the signal, rounded to 50 points.
Option premiums are modelled with Black-Scholes using India VIX as the volatility (each minute's range uses that minute's closing India VIX) and a 6.5% risk-free rate.
Slippage of 0.5 points is applied to every fill.
Charges are applied at today's rates for the whole period.
Only one position is open at a time.
Missing market data is never filled in; minutes and days without data are skipped.

disclosures.modelled_premiums_text: Premiums modelled, not actual. Nikasha has no historical option prices, so every option price in this report is calculated from the index level and India VIX. Real prices, and so real results, would differ.
disclosures.volatility_limitation_text: India VIX measures expected 30-day volatility for near-the-money options. It doesn't capture how far-from-the-money options or options close to expiry are priced, so results for expiry-day trades and far strikes are the least reliable.
disclosures.costs_note_text: Costs use the rates you confirmed, which are today's rates. Charges were different in earlier years, and that change isn't modelled.
